free_tier.stated: Free: 50,000 executions and 500,000 events ingested per month, 5 concurrent steps, no credit card required
free_tier.notes: An execution is one function run or one step execution, so a run with five steps uses six. The Free plan also allows 3 active workspaces, 5 apps per workspace, 100 functions per app and 2 active branch deploys; a run may last 30 days including sleeps. Function code runs on the user's own host, which Inngest calls.

per_object_cap.stated: 256 KiB per event; 32 MiB of function run state

retention.stated: trace and log history: 24 hours on Free

egress.terms: not applicable: Inngest calls the user's function endpoints; no traffic allowance is published

interface_detail: REST API at api.inngest.com (v1 stable, v2 stable in development) for events, function runs and environments; every endpoint is also exposed in the Inngest CLI
tooling: the Inngest SDKs in the user's app, the Inngest CLI (inngest api) and the local dev server (npx inngest-cli dev). As a last resort the open-source server can be installed and run by the user on a rented or free machine.
chaining: Adds retries, schedules, sleeps and fan-out to functions served from a free serverless host, so it composes with a free compute tier that has no queue or cron of its own.

limits.value: 24 hours of trace and log history

limits_note: 5 concurrent steps, queue depth 100,000, event batches of 5 with a 30-second batch timeout. A step may run up to 2 hours, subject to the host's shorter timeout. Since October 20, 2026 executions in runs with checkpointing are no longer undercounted, so a Free account may reach the cap sooner.
binding_note: 50,000 executions a month binds first, and each step counts, so multi-step functions reach it in fewer runs.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up form asks for an email address and a password, or GitHub or Google sign-in; the free tier needs no card.

reliability_note: Since October 20, 2026 executions in checkpointed runs count in full, so a Free account can hit its cap sooner than before.
confidence_note: Plan limits and sign-up fields are read on first-party pages; the REST API answered HTTP 401 to a request without a key. A function run is not measured.
